question: Gombrich's history of art begins: 'There really is no such thing as Art.' What did he mean?
answer: That there are only artists: people who, in different times and places, made pictures and statues for many reasons. Gombrich warned that Art with a capital A can become a bogey and a fetish; better to look at each work and ask what its makers were trying to do.
move: Look at what each maker was trying to do, not at labels.
simply: Gombrich said Art isn't one big thing. There are just people who made things, for all kinds of reasons, each worth looking at on its own terms.
why: It frees you to enjoy art without a rulebook or permission: look closely, and ask what the maker wanted.

book.title: The Story of Art
book.author: E. H. Gombrich
book.badge: In print since 1950, now in its sixteenth edition
